scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning:
The scenario involves a stepbrother who created a profile on the user's Nintendo Switch during a period of babysitting. The user later deleted that profile, resulting in the loss of the stepbrother's game progress (Zelda save). The stepbrother became upset, and the user's father criticized the action as mean.

Key considerations:
- The profile was created for the stepbrother's use during a specific time when the user needed to babysit.
- Deleting the profile removed the stepbrother's game progress, causing emotional distress.
- The user's primary reason for deletion was personal convenience (avoiding extra clicks), not necessity.
- The stepbrother had developed an attachment to the game and was enjoying it.
- The user acknowledges they usually don't bring the Switch over when visiting, suggesting the profile wasn't needed for ongoing shared use.

Morally, the action seems inconsiderate because:
- It disregarded the stepbrother's enjoyment and emotional investment in the game.
- The deletion was unnecessary for the user's own use, as they could have simply not used the Switch during visits or kept the profile without inconvenience.
- It caused harm (distress) to a family member for a trivial reason (saving a few clicks).
- The user had initially allowed the profile to foster a positive relationship and assist with babysitting, so deleting it abruptly breaks that trust.

While the Switch is the user's property and they have the right to manage it, morally the action is questionable due to the lack of consideration for others' feelings and the disproportionate impact relative to the benefit.

Thus, the action is morally unacceptable.
